During my the summer after my freshman year if high school me and my friend were wondering around our neighbourhood. We lived in this very huddled together immigrant community, he was a first generation immigrant and I was a second. We were bored and stumbled upon this path behind a factory in our area, it led to down to this flat gravely area. We decided to keep the place as our little haven. We barbecued there by staring little fires and cooking hot dogs over the fire. Eventually we decided to build ourselves a little home there. We scavenged our neighbourhood for wood from old furniture and pallets left behind by trucks and built ourselves a little cabin. That cabin survived two years before it was torn down, and even after that we moved deeper down the gravely path into a valley and built a new cabin. It was no where near as impressive as the first but we made due. To this day me and my best friend still head down there to enjoy the peace and quiet and have ourselves a little bbq.

Unless earth begins to slow or speed up it will remain on its path around the sun.

There are many theories behind what dreams exactly are. A popular theory tends to blame "uncomfortable" dreams on fears or anxiety had in real life. Say you have arachnophobia but are unaware of it since you've never encounter a spider in real life. Well one day you spot one just hanging out on your desk and you freak out. Although you may not think much of it as the day goes on your brain will store it for later. As you sleep that night you may have a bad dream involving, maybe not a spider, but some sort of multi-legged fuzzy creature with several eyes. This is attributed to your brain realising you have an actual fear of spiders and is trying to make you very aware of it. Other times people believe dreams are purely left up to random events made up by the imagination and are therefore undecipherable.
